interest: This file is uniquely valuable to historians of pre-World War II U.S.–Japanese relations because it documents the acute micro-diplomatic and intelligence friction surrounding Japanese maritime activities in strategic North Pacific and Philippine waters. Ostensibly routine requests for fishery training ships and scientific research vessels (such as the Hakuyo Maru and Hakuho Maru) to investigate fur seal migration under the 1911 Fur Seals Convention or inspect fishing grounds triggered intense interdepartmental debates among the State, Navy, War, Commerce, Treasury, and Interior Departments. The records reveal deep American suspicions that Japan was conducting hydrographic reconnaissance, probing closed military/naval zones in the Aleutians (Attu, Amchitka, and Atka), and encroaching upon Alaskan salmon fisheries in Bristol Bay, illustrating the fragile balance between diplomatic conciliation and national security surveillance in the Pacific prior to 1941.
overview: This file comprises the State Department's official List of Papers (purport and docket register sheets, pages 25 through 37) for decimal file 894.628 (Fisheries / Fishing Vessels: Japan) covering sub-numbers 168 through 240 between July 1936 and May 1939. The documents index and summarize extensive diplomatic exchanges between the Japanese Embassy in Washington and the Department of State, as well as interdepartmental coordination involving the Navy, War, Commerce (Bureau of Fisheries), Treasury (Coast Guard and Customs), Interior, and Labor departments, and consular reporting from Tokyo and Yokohama. Major subjects include Japanese requests for training and research vessels—predominantly the Hakuyo Maru, Hakuho Maru, Shirotaka Maru, Itobuki Maru, and Shonan Maru—to enter U.S. territorial waters, visit closed islands (such as St. Paul in the Pribilofs and Attu, Amchitka, and Atka in the Aleutians), conduct fur seal migration research under the 1911 Fur Seals Convention, call at Philippine ports (Manila, Davao, Zamboanga), and visit Dutch Harbor and Honolulu. The file tracks U.S. policy decisions balancing diplomatic courtesies against strategic security concerns, immigration and customs regulations, and domestic anxieties over Japanese encroachment on Alaskan salmon and seal resources.

subfiles.about: List of Papers docket sheet indexing entries 168 to 174 regarding Japanese vessels Hakuho Maru, Hakuyo Maru, Tenyo Maru, Shirotaka Maru, and Itobuki Maru.
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet indexes State Department correspondence from July 14, 1936, to February 23, 1937, for file 894.628. It records the Japanese Embassy's notification that the Hakuho Maru's proposed visit to the Aleutian Islands was abandoned, followed by notifications to the War and Treasury Departments discontinuing courtesy privileges. It also lists Coast Guard patrol reports from the Cyane and Alert regarding the Hakuyo Maru and Tenyo Maru, a Commerce Department report citing the Pacific Fisherman on Japanese fishing off Alaska, a letter of thanks transmitted by Ambassador Grew for the Shirotaka Maru's visit, and inquiries concerning the Itobuki Maru's planned visit to Manila.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Page 25: Entries 168–174 (July 1936 – February 1937)

subfiles.about: List of Papers docket sheet indexing entries 174 to 178 regarding courtesies for the Itobuki Maru at Manila and the Hakuyo Maru's proposed Alaskan cruise.
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet indexes correspondence between February 23 and March 30, 1937. It records interdepartmental clearance with the War and Navy Departments granting courtesies for the Japanese Fisheries Experimental Station vessel Itobuki Maru to visit Manila in March 1937. It also tracks Japanese Embassy Note No. 55 requesting permission for the Tokyo Fishing Institute training ship Hakuyo Maru, under Captain Jinzo Nakagawa, to visit Bristol Bay, St. Paul Island, and Dutch Harbor, prompting the Navy Department and State Department to request specific justifications for visiting the closed port of St. Paul Island.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Page 26: Entries 174–178 (February – March 1937)

subfiles.about: List of Papers docket sheet indexing entries 179 to 184 regarding proposed visits of the Hakuyo Maru and Hakuho Maru to Alaska and the Aleutians.
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet covers records from April 6 to May 10, 1937, concerning Japanese public vessels seeking access to Alaskan waters. Consul General Garrels in Tokyo transmits communications exchanged with the Fisheries Institute regarding the Hakuyo Maru, while the Japanese Embassy asserts that the vessel's visit to St. Paul Island is for scientific study of fur seal breeding conditions. Simultaneously, the Japanese Embassy requests permission under Note No. 93 for the Hakuho Maru to visit Chichagof, Constantine, and Nazan Bay in the Aleutians to trace seal migration from Asia, which encounters strong opposition from the Navy and Commerce Departments.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Page 27: Entries 179–184 (April – May 1937)

subfiles.about: List of Papers docket sheet indexing entries 184 to 188 restricting the Hakuyo Maru's itinerary and denying the Hakuho Maru access to the Aleutians.
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet records communications from May 10 to May 15, 1937. It documents the State Department's formal decision granting the Hakuyo Maru permission to visit Dutch Harbor while strictly withholding permission for St. Paul Island and warning against entering U.S. territorial waters in Bristol Bay. It also registers unanimous recommendations from the Navy and Interior Departments denying the Hakuho Maru's proposed visits to western Aleutian harbors, and notes coordination with the Governor of Alaska and Commanding General of the Ninth Corps Area.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Page 28: Entries 184–188 (May 1937)

subfiles.about: List of Papers docket sheet indexing entries 188 to 194 detailing the reconsideration and approval of the Hakuyo Maru's visit to St. Paul Island.
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet indexes entries from May 19 to June 4, 1937. Following further explanations from the Japanese Embassy in Note No. 112, the State Department reversed its prior refusal and granted permission on June 1 for the Hakuyo Maru to visit St. Paul Island on July 12–13 as an exceptional, non-precedential courtesy. Consul General Garrels reports from Tokyo that the ship has already departed Japanese waters, requiring telegraphic notice to authorities at St. Paul to amend visa and health documents, while the War and Treasury Departments report on the denial of the Hakuho Maru.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Page 29: Entries 188–194 (May – June 1937)

subfiles.about: List of Papers docket sheet indexing entries 195 to 200 regarding customs waivers, immigration courtesies, and Fur Seals Convention discussions.
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet covers records from May 19 to June 14, 1937. It notes Treasury decisions waiving entry fees, clearance, and tonnage tax for the Hakuyo Maru at Dutch Harbor, alongside coordination with the Labor and War Departments. It also documents an internal State Department memorandum by Joseph W. Ballantine recounting a conference with Commander Hill (Navy) and Ward T. Bower (Bureau of Fisheries) where they agreed to refuse the Hakuho Maru's Aleutian itinerary under the 1911 Fur Seals Convention while sympathetically reconsidering the Hakuyo Maru, leading to a new Japanese Embassy note renewing requests or proposing an alternate stop at Dutch Harbor.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Page 30: Entries 195–200 (May – June 1937)

subfiles.about: List of Papers docket sheet indexing entries 200 to 204 regarding Navy objections to the Hakuho Maru in the Aleutians and clearance for Dutch Harbor.
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet indexes entries from May 17 to June 19, 1937. It records a memorandum by William T. Turner of the Far Eastern Division proposing interdepartmental consultations regarding the Hakuho Maru's seal migration survey, as well as reports from Consul General Garrels on visas granted for Dutch Harbor, Nome, and Unalaska. It documents the Navy Department's firm position that visits to western Aleutian harbors cannot be permitted under the Fur Seals Convention, though an arrival at Dutch Harbor around June 30 is acceptable provided exact arrival and departure dates are reported.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Page 31: Entries 200–204 (May – June 1937)

subfiles.about: List of Papers docket sheet indexing entries 205 to 210 regarding the Shonan Maru's Philippine mission and final arrangements for the Hakuho Maru.
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet indexes correspondence from June 11 to June 29, 1937. It records Japanese Embassy Note No. 130 requesting permission for the fisheries vessel Shonan Maru to visit Manila, Davao, and Zamboanga to investigate shipping and fishing industries, which received clearance from the Commerce, War, and Navy Departments. It also registers the State Department's formal note of June 25 denying the Hakuho Maru's Aleutian visits while permitting a Dutch Harbor visit from June 30 to July 2, 1937, with customs courtesies arranged via Juneau.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Page 32: Entries 205–210 (June 1937)

subfiles.about: List of Papers docket sheet indexing entries 211 to 218 tracking schedule modifications and courtesies for the Shonan Maru across Philippine ports.
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet indexes entries from July 7 to October 21, 1937. It records U.S. approval of the Shonan Maru's visit to the Philippines and documents subsequent Japanese Embassy notes (Nos. 165 and 171) adjusting the vessel's arrival dates at Manila, Davao, and Zamboanga during August and September 1937. Interdepartmental coordination with the War Department (notifying the Commanding General, Philippine Department) and Commerce Department is tracked, concluding with letters of acknowledgment and thanks in October.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Page 33: Entries 211–218 (July – October 1937)

subfiles.about: List of Papers docket sheet indexing entries 218 to 224 on the Hakuyo Maru's Manila visit and renewed Japanese requests for the Aleutian Islands.
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet indexes records from October 28, 1937, to May 4, 1938. It details interdepartmental approvals by the Navy and War Departments for the Tokyo Fishing Institute vessel Hakuyo Maru to visit Manila in January 1938, including a minor schedule modification. It also records Japanese Embassy Note No. 69 of May 2, 1938, requesting permission for the vessel (Hakuho Maru) to visit Attu and Atka Islands for supplies, seal migration research, and supervision of poaching, which prompted Far Eastern Division officer Leo D. Sturgeon to recommend interdepartmental consultations.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Page 34: Entries 218–224 (October 1937 – May 1938)

subfiles.about: First copy of docket sheet 35 indexing entries 224 to 227 on conditional clearance and surveillance for the Hakuho Maru's 1938 Aleutian cruise.
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet (first version of sheet 35) indexes correspondence from May 7 to May 25, 1938, regarding Japanese Embassy Note No. 69. It documents Navy Department opinions and circular notifications recommending conditional permission for the Hakuho Maru under possible U.S. naval or Coast Guard surveillance in view of sensitive conditions in Bristol Bay. It notes the State Department's reply of May 20 granting access to Unalaska as the sole open port for supplies and shelter on a non-precedential basis, alongside arrangements by the Labor and Treasury Departments.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Page 35 (Copy 1): Entries 224–227 (May 1938)

subfiles.about: Second copy of docket sheet 35 indexing entries 224 to 227 highlighting Commerce Department recommendations for the Hakuho Maru.
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet (second version of sheet 35) indexes entries from May 7 to May 25, 1938, providing a more detailed record of the Commerce Department's May 9 response. The Commerce Department reported no scientific justification for the Hakuho Maru to visit the Aleutians since fur seals were not found there, but recommended granting permission under naval or Coast Guard supervision due to Japanese fisheries activities in Bristol Bay. The sheet records the resulting circular note, State Department conditional approval for Unalaska, and Labor and Treasury confirmations.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Page 35 (Copy 2): Entries 224–227 (May 1938)

subfiles.about: First copy of docket sheet 36 indexing entries 228 to 238 on interdepartmental conferences and approvals for the Hakuyo Maru's 1939 Pacific cruise.
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet indexes correspondence from May 28, 1938, to April 25, 1939. It records a State Department memorandum regarding conferences with Commander Struble (Navy) and Mr. Bower (Commerce) concerning the Hakuho Maru, as well as Interior Department notices to the Governor of Alaska. It also indexes Japanese Embassy Note No. 69 of April 3, 1939, requesting permission for the Hakuyo Maru to visit St. Paul Island, Dutch Harbor, and Honolulu, alongside swift clearances and instructions issued by the Labor, War (Commanding General, Hawaii), Interior, Commerce, and Treasury Departments.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Page 36 (marked Page 35, Copy 1): Entries 228–238 (May 1938 – April 1939)

subfiles.about: Second copy of docket sheet 36 indexing entries 228 to 238 highlighting War Department limitations and 1939 Hakuyo Maru clearances.
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet (variant typing of sheet 36) indexes records from May 1938 to April 1939. It highlights the War Department's May 28 statement that it had no personnel or installations on Attu or Atka Islands to extend facilities to the visiting Japanese vessel. It further catalogs interdepartmental clearances across April 1939 from the Labor, War, Interior, Commerce, and Treasury Departments approving the Hakuyo Maru's proposed summer 1939 itinerary encompassing St. Paul Island, Dutch Harbor, and Honolulu.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Page 36 (marked Page 35, Copy 2): Entries 228–238 (May 1938 – April 1939)

subfiles.about: List of Papers docket sheet indexing entries 239 to 240 recording Navy Department approval and final authorization for the Hakuyo Maru's 1939 cruise.
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet indexes records from April 27 to May 24, 1939, concluding the registered entries for file 894.628. It documents the Navy Department's formal approval for the Hakuyo Maru to visit St. Paul Island, Dutch Harbor, and Honolulu, noting that while St. Paul was not a port of entry, the Fur Seals Treaty implied a right to visit seal breeding grounds. It concludes with the State Department's telegram No. 141 of May 24, 1939, granting permission and instructing that the U.S. Consulate at Yokohama be notified.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Page 37: Entries 239–240 (April – May 1939)
